ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three blue slanted lines marked with pink arrow marks, indicating that these three slanted lines are mutually parallel. There is also a blue transversal slanting upward to the right and an approximately vertical blue transversal intersecting these parallel lines. The figure marks the angles (7x+9)°, (7y−4)°, (11x−1)°, (2y+5)°, and the required z°. Reasoning: According to the angle relationships between the parallel lines and the transversals in the figure, (7x+9)° and (7y−4)° form a pair of adjacent supplementary angles, so (7x+9)+(7y−4)=180, which simplifies to x+y=25. At the vertical transversal, (11x−1)° and (2y+5)° are also supplementary angles, so (11x−1)+(2y+5)=180, which simplifies to 11x+2y=176. Substitute y=25−x into the second equation: 11x+2(25−x)=176, 9x+50=176, 9x=126, x=14; thus y=11. In the figure z is equal to (7y−4)°, therefore z=7y−4=7(11)−4=73.

On the vertical transversal cutting two of the parallel lines, the angles labeled (11x−1)° and (2y+5)° are supplementary, so set (11x−1)+(2y+5)=180. Solve these two equations to get x=14 and y=11. Then use the fact that z is vertical/opposite to the angle labeled (7y−4)° at the upper intersection, so z=7y−4=73.
